title: Applied anatomy: the breast, axillary node levels and sentinel node biopsy

guidelineVersions: NICE NG101 (published 18 July 2018; last updated 14 April 2025)

related.why: The axilla and brachial plexus in more depth
Interpreting the core biopsy report for the same kind of cancer
Consenting for wide local excision and sentinel node biopsy

brief.scenario: Mrs Helen Marchetti, 52, has an invasive breast cancer in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast. Axillary ultrasound is normal. She is planned for wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the anatomy of the breast and axilla and its relevance to her surgery.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Breast, drainage, levels by pectoralis minor, nerves to protect, then what NICE says about the axilla.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling the sentinel node 'a level I node': it is defined by drainage, not level.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The levels are defined by pectoralis minor: lateral, behind, medial."

flow: Extent and support of the breast

grid.label: Extent and support of the breast
grid.fail: Cannot describe where the breast lies.
grid.pass: Ribs 2 to 6, sternum to midaxillary line, on pectoralis major and serratus anterior, with an axillary tail.
grid.high: Adds the retromammary space and suspensory ligaments; tumour tethering them causes skin dimpling.

grid.label: Lymphatic drainage
grid.fail: Cannot name where breast lymph drains.
grid.pass: Most drains to the axillary nodes; medial tissue also drains to internal thoracic (mammary) nodes.
grid.high: Knows an internal mammary sentinel node can appear on lymphoscintigraphy, because drainage does not follow fixed levels.

grid.label: Axillary levels
grid.fail: Cannot define the levels or name the muscle that defines them.
grid.pass: Level I lateral to pectoralis minor, level II behind it, level III medial to it.
grid.high: Places interpectoral (Rotter's) nodes between the pectorals and names level III as infraclavicular, a sign of more advanced disease.

grid.label: Nerves at risk in axillary surgery
grid.fail: Cannot name a nerve at risk in the axilla.
grid.pass: Long thoracic (winged scapula), thoracodorsal (latissimus dorsi weakness), intercostobrachial (numb medial upper arm).
grid.high: Adds the medial pectoral nerve to pectoralis major, and describes where the long thoracic and thoracodorsal nerves run.

grid.label: Sentinel node biopsy
grid.fail: Says sentinel node biopsy samples level I, or plans clearance for a normal axilla.
grid.pass: Normal ultrasound or negative needle biopsy: sentinel node biopsy rather than clearance, using isotope and blue dye.
grid.high: Explains the sentinel node is the first node draining the tumour, found by drainage wherever it lies.

grid.label: Further axillary treatment
grid.fail: Clears the axilla for any positive node, including micrometastases.
grid.pass: Biopsy-proven node before surgery: clearance. Sentinel macrometastasis: clearance or radiotherapy. Micrometastases or isolated tumour cells: nothing further.
grid.high: After breast conservation with 1 or 2 macrometastases and planned radiotherapy and systemic therapy, discusses omitting further axillary treatment.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: On the chest. I'm not sure of the exact extent.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Level I is the lowest and level III the highest, I think. I'm not sure what defines them.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How do you stage her axilla?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Sentinel node biopsy takes the level I nodes.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Ribs 2 to 6, sternum to midaxillary line, on pectoralis major and serratus anterior, with an axillary tail.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mostly axillary, and medially to the internal thoracic nodes.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: They're defined by pectoralis minor: level I lateral, II behind, III medial.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Long thoracic, winged scapula; thoracodorsal, latissimus dorsi weakness; intercostobrachial, numb medial arm.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How do you stage her axilla?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Ultrasound is normal, so sentinel node biopsy rather than clearance, with isotope and blue dye.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The sentinel node has a macrometastasis.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Further axillary treatment: clearance or radiotherapy. Micrometastases or isolated tumour cells: nothing further.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Tumour tethers the suspensory ligaments running to the skin. Behind the breast is the retromammary space.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Lymphoscintigraphy shows an internal mammary hot spot.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Drainage doesn't respect levels; medial drainage can reach the internal thoracic chain.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I, II and III by pectoralis minor; Rotter's nodes between the pectorals; level III is infraclavicular and means more advanced disease.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Where do the nerves you protect run?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Long thoracic on serratus anterior, thoracodorsal with its vessels to latissimus. The medial pectoral nerve supplies pectoralis major.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Is the sentinel node level I?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Usually, but it's defined as the first node draining the tumour, wherever it lies.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: One macrometastasis after wide local excision.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: She's having whole-breast radiotherapy and systemic therapy, so I'd discuss omitting further axillary treatment.

failures.move: Not identifying the long thoracic and thoracodorsal nerves at operation.
failures.consequence: Risks a winged scapula or latissimus weakness.

failures.move: Equating the sentinel node with level I.
failures.consequence: A sentinel node elsewhere is missed and the axilla understaged.

recovery.line: Let me start from pectoralis minor: lateral is I, behind is II, medial is III.
Most drains to the axilla; I wouldn't quote a figure I can't source.

knowledge.fact: Breast: ribs 2 to 6, sternum to midaxillary line, on pectoralis major and serratus anterior.
Long thoracic nerve on serratus anterior; thoracodorsal to latissimus dorsi; intercostobrachial crosses the axilla.
Normal ultrasound or negative biopsy: sentinel node biopsy, isotope and blue dye.
Preoperative positive biopsy: clearance. Sentinel macrometastasis: clearance or radiotherapy. Micrometastases or isolated tumour cells: none.

recall.think: Understaging the axilla, or lymphoedema from unnecessary clearance.
recall.say: "Levels by pectoralis minor; the sentinel node is defined by drainage."
do: Sentinel node biopsy with isotope and blue dye
Protect long thoracic and thoracodorsal nerves

numbers.meaning: Sentinel macrometastases where omitting further axillary treatment is discussed

recall.trap: 'Sentinel node biopsy is a level I sample.'
recall.finish: Wide local excision and sentinel node biopsy; MDT decides further axillary treatment.

partner.opening: "This woman is having a sentinel node biopsy. Describe the breast: where it lies and what supports it."
partner.actorBrief: You are the examiner. Start with the breast, then work down the push questions. Press if the candidate calls the sentinel node a level I node.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about axillary staging so far
reveals.finding: Axillary ultrasound normal; no needle biopsy needed.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the sentinel node result
reveals.finding: One sentinel node with a 4 mm macrometastasis.

push.question: Define the axillary levels.
push.expect: By pectoralis minor: lateral, behind, medial.

push.question: Which nerves do you protect, and what happens if each is injured?
push.expect: Long thoracic, thoracodorsal, intercostobrachial with deficits.

push.question: How do you find the sentinel node?
push.expect: Isotope and blue dye; first draining node wherever it lies.

push.question: What if it is positive?
push.expect: Macrometastasis: clearance or radiotherapy, or discussion if 1 or 2 after BCS; micrometastasis: nothing further.

curveballs.prompt: The sentinel node is found in level II.
curveballs.safeAnswer: It is still the sentinel node; remove and examine it.
Long thoracic nerve injury, serratus anterior weakness.

curveballs.prompt: What proportion of lymph goes to the axilla?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Most; declines to quote an unsourced figure.
